body.statement: For every \(K\geq2\), the function \(p_{\mathrm{corner}}\) satisfies \(\Pr_R\{p_{\mathrm{corner}}(C)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\) for every \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). Its nontrivial value is \(\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\), which can be strictly below \(1/2\).
body.justification: This analytic counterpoint prevents the group classification from being misread as nonexistence of all other exact weak-null tests.
body.gap: Exact binary procedures in \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} already show that nuisance-aware tests can exist; this proposition isolates a particularly transparent non-orbit rule inside the present model.
body.consumer: It tells DeclareDesign developers that an exact weak-null module may use analytic calibration or nuisance maximization even though common-orbit ranks are coarse.
